findings.reason: the plan must thread the selected `desc_2d` (or the selection) into vessel extraction, or state why the index cannot differ for its inputs.
findings.text: `extract_geometry` picks its wall data from `_select_description_2d(wall_ids)` (extract.py:322, returns `descs[best_idx]`, which is not necessarily `[0]`), but the function the plan fills the new field from, `extract_vessel_shells`, hardcodes `wall_ids.description_2d[0]` (walls.py:175); on a machine whose richest `description_2d` is not index 0 (the WEST `desc[1]` mobile case the selector exists for), the vessel field would describe a different `description_2d` than `wall_units`

findings.reason: naming the render owner decides where the draw lives and whether the altair geometry path is in scope.
findings.text: the plan describes `geometry_figure_mpl` drawing each shell as a line without citing the rendering owner it must extend: components are dataclasses in `imas_ink/components.py` (e.g. `WallOutline`, components.py:138) dispatched by `render_mpl` (mpl.py:87) and `render_alt` (alt.py:91); the 2D geometry draw sites are a census of two, `geometry_figure_mpl` (figures.py:181) and `equilibrium_chart_alt` (figures.py:702), the latter building its own `WallOutline` and using the altair registry, so a draw added only in `geometry_figure_mpl` reaches neither the altair path nor any future component-level addition

findings.reason: naming `imas_ink/mpl.py` as the owner makes the change an extension of one dispatch pair rather than a second plot call that drifts from it.
findings.text: an inline draw of `VesselShell.r/.z` in `geometry_figure_mpl` reproduces `_render_wall_mpl` (mpl.py:360), which already plots a list of `(r, z)` units with `InkStyle.wall_color/wall_linewidth`; the vessel shells are `WallOutline2D` instances (walls.py:27/42) with exactly that `r`/`z` shape, so the honest change is to extend the `render_mpl`/`render_alt` dispatch pair rather than fork the plotting

findings.reason: JT-60SA writes `annular.outline_inner/outline_outer`, the path the plan adds, so the dead fallback does not affect the target figures.
findings.text: the plan states the extractor falls back to "a plain `outline`" and leaves that path unchanged, but the DD defines the vessel polygon at `wall/description_2d/vessel/unit/element/outline`, not `unit.outline`, so the fallback reads an attribute that does not exist and is unreachable; the plan preserves a dead branch and should either correct it to `element.outline` or record that it is out of scope

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v3 §1 extends _render_wall_mpl/_render_wall_alt rather than adding an inline plot in geometry_figure_mpl

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v3 §1: extract_vessel_shells takes the description_2d entry, and extract_geometry passes the one _select_description_2d chose, so vessel and limiter come from the same entry

reuse_search-2.reason: plan v3 §1 draws through the component dispatch: WallOutline gains the vessel shells and _render_wall_mpl and _render_wall_alt draw them, reaching geometry_figure_mpl and equilibrium_chart_alt

reuse_search-3.reason: the reviewer marks it not plan-changing: the unit.outline fallback is a pre-existing branch this plan neither relies on nor changes; plan v3 §1 records that the Data Dictionary places the polygon on unit.element[*].outline and leaves the correction out of scope
